name: species-area-and-isolation
title: The species-area law and the isolation gradient
question:
Under the canonical MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium model, do the two central
predictions emerge as quantitative laws — (1) equilibrium richness grows with
island area as a power law S ~ A^z (Arrhenius 1921; Preston 1962), and (2)
equilibrium richness declines monotonically with isolation distance?
hypothesis:
In the extinction-limited regime, S* ~ A^(area_exponent), so a log-spaced area
gradient at fixed isolation should give a straight line on log-log axes with
slope z ~ area_exponent. Separately, because colonization c = c0/(1+distance)
falls hyperbolically with distance, a distance gradient at fixed area should
give richness that drops steeply then plateaus — a monotone decline (rank
correlation strongly negative).
objective:
Measure (a) the species-area slope z from a log-log fit over an area gradient
(isolation fixed), and (b) the Spearman rank correlation of richness with
isolation distance over a distance gradient (area fixed), each on an 8-seed
ensemble mean, and render the species-area and species-distance curves.
description:
This study turns the two qualitative predictions of island biogeography into
measured laws using the mw_equilibrium composite. The area gradient isolates
the extinction side (larger islands lose species less often -> more species);
the distance gradient isolates the colonization side (farther islands receive
fewer colonists -> fewer species). It builds on mw-equilibrium-reproduction,
which established that the process sits on the equilibrium rate curves.

expected_behavior.name: species-area-law
expected_behavior.en:
Equilibrium richness increases with island area as a power law S ~ A^z with
a clearly positive slope on log-log axes.
expected_behavior.rationale:
Larger islands carry larger per-species populations and so lose species less
often; in the extinction-limited regime S* ~ A^(area_exponent).

expected_behavior.name: isolation-declines
expected_behavior.en:
Equilibrium richness declines monotonically with isolation distance (strong
negative rank correlation).
expected_behavior.rationale:
colonization c = c0/(1+distance) falls with isolation, lowering the
immigration curve and so the equilibrium S*.

behavior_tests.name: species-area-law
behavior_tests.description: Log-log species-area slope z must be clearly positive (> 0.08).

provenance.note:
Measured z = 0.12 (area gradient 1-100, isolation 0, 8-seed ensemble).
Within the low end of the empirical 0.1-0.35 band; large islands approach
pool saturation, which flattens the slope.

behavior_tests.name: isolation-declines
behavior_tests.description: Spearman rank corr(distance, richness) must be below -0.9.

provenance.note:
Measured Spearman = -0.97 (distance gradient 0-30 at fixed area 30,
8-seed ensemble). Pearson is only -0.79 because the c=c0/(1+d) decline is
hyperbolic; rank correlation captures the monotonicity.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
With both laws reproduced, the model is validated against the two canonical
MacArthur-Wilson predictions and is ready to be extended (neutral theory,
microbial regimes, trophic / general-dynamic-model follow-ups).

canonical_runs.name: default
canonical_runs.label: Species-area z-fit + isolation decline (area & distance gradients, 8-seed)

conclusion:
Both canonical predictions emerge as measured laws. Richness grows with area
as S ~ A^z with z = 0.12 (area gradient, isolation fixed), and declines
monotonically with isolation (Spearman -0.97; the hyperbolic colonization
kernel makes the decline sharp-then-plateau, which Pearson -0.79 understates).
Area acts through extinction and isolation through colonization, exactly as the
two-curve theory predicts.

findings.statement: Both canonical predictions emerge as laws: richness grows with area as a power law S ~ A^z (z = 0.12) and declines monotonically with isolation (Spearman -0.97) - area acting through extinction, isolation through colonization.

derived.insight: Both canonical predictions emerge as laws: richness grows with area as a power law S ~ A^z (z = 0.12) and declines monotonically with isolation (Spearman -0.97) - area acting through extinction, isolation through colonization.
